properties.name: The environment compliance layer is built: a design can say what rules its operating environment imposes, whether it complies, and be asked when it has not said
properties.rationale:
The distinction this layer carries is the reason it was worth building rather than retiring: a rule the design cannot argue with is a different kind of thing from a budget it set itself or a convention it chose, and only the third is dictated by the world. reflow2 uses the middle kind heavily and had never used the third at all.

WHY NOW AND NOT BEFORE. The 2026-08-26 parking was correct on its own evidence: three field reports that month mentioned environment compliance zero times, and building on a document's argument alone is the opposite of how everything else here has been decided. What changed is not the argument but the asking. The contract-and-standards brainstorm names "building codes" and "standards", both of which are values in this type's own rule_type enum, written months earlier by somebody who had the same thought.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not make anyone record a regulation, and it cannot check that a stated rule is real or that a claimed compliance is true — a passing claim is recorded, never validated, which is the standing non-goal. What it removes is the reason a design could not say any of it.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Declared in schema/environment.yaml since 2026-07-17. Parked 2026-08-26 as option (e) of five, because parking was the only disposition free to reverse and no user had asked. The parking named its own condition — a real request — and on 2026-09-07 Anthony asked, then ruled: build the whole leg.

ALL THREE LEGS TOGETHER, because a write side without a read side is the failure this project has measured repeatedly, and the deliberation recorded that objection against the write-side-only option before the decision was taken.

THE VOCABULARY, now writable: add_environment_rule records a rule the design CANNOT NEGOTIATE, carrying authority (who issues it), jurisdiction (where it applies), reference (the citation), and mandatory. Three kinds of rule stay distinct — a Constraint is self-imposed, a DesignRule is a chosen convention, an EnvironmentRule is imposed by the world. operates_in, imposes, complies_with and violates_rule draw the four edges; every one of them previously required the generic escape hatch, and OPERATES_IN already had three edges written that way, which was the first evidence anyone had reached for this vocabulary. set_violation_status triages a flagged violation and REWRITES the edge rather than removing it, because the record of what was found and what was decided is the audit trail.

THE TWO DETECTORS. unchecked_compliance fires once per MANDATORY rule nothing has answered — neither complied with nor violated — because a design that has not said whether it meets a code has not met it. An advisory rule is not asked about; mandatory is the load-bearing flag and absent reads as mandatory, since a rule whose force nobody stated is not safely assumed to be advice. open_violation fires per flagged edge still reading `proposed`, severity-weighted, and closes when somebody grants a variance or calls it a defect.

SCOPING, stated because it is a judgement: unchecked_compliance is keyed PER RULE, not per (element, rule) pair. A design with 234 capabilities and 10 rules would otherwise raise 2,340 findings, which is the hub-shaped noise that got the overtaken-defect detector narrowed the week it shipped. open_violation is deliberately NOT aggregate: a violation is a specific claim about a specific element with three possible answers, and collapsing several would ask them as one unanswerable question.

FAILING FIRST, OBSERVED: five core tests written before any of it existed, failing first on the missing edge CONSTANTS — the layer was dormant down to the names.

AND THE REACHABILITY MAP GAINED THE WRITERS IT WAS MISSING. Adding a `severity` parameter to violates_rule made DriftEvent.severity read as newly reachable, because an unmapped type falls back to the whole surface — the cross-type leak arriving through the fallback path rather than the pool. The reconcile family is now mapped to DriftEvent and the compliance tools to EnvironmentRule, which surfaced DriftEvent.summary as a further machine-written property and it was classified rather than let slide.
